summary: The last 4 weeks have been severely disrupted by illness from around 2 August, with training effectively halted for approximately 10 days and sleep quality collapsing dramatically (multiple nights under 5 hours, body battery routinely hitting single digits). Only three sessions were logged in the entire window — a hard run on 18 July, a long ride on 20 July, and a leisure hike on 25 July — leaving a significant fitness gap heading into the final build for the Half Oceanman (49 days away). The priority now is a careful, staged return to training, protecting sleep and recovery above all else, before cautiously rebuilding volume across weeks 9–11.
suggestions: Treat the week of 15–17 August as a genuine return-from-illness week, not a training week: the Saturday ride should be capped at 35–40 km at 120–140W and the Sunday run replaced with an easy 30–35 min walk/jog — body battery on 15 Aug is recorded at 0, which is a hard stop signal.

Enforce a sleep gate for all intensity sessions over the next 10 days: if the previous night's sleep was under 6 hours or body battery on waking is below 45, convert any planned quality session (intervals, tempo, race-pace) to an easy aerobic alternative or full rest.

The Half Oceanman (5,000m swim in 49 days) is the nearest race and swim volume in the plan is the weakest link — prioritise getting two pool or open-water sessions per week back in from week 9 onwards, even if that means shortening a ride or run to protect recovery.

The week of 24 August abroad: confirm bike access in advance; if no bike is available, the 29 August 100 km ride should automatically become a 75-min open-water or pool swim rather than being skipped entirely, keeping Half Oceanman swim volume on track.

Monitor running HR carefully on return — your 18 July 5 km averaged 179 bpm at only 5:02/km pace, suggesting cardiovascular stress or pre-illness fatigue even before the illness began; keep all running in weeks 8–9 truly aerobic (HR cap 145 bpm) before reintroducing any race-pace work.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk8 Long Ride (AI adjusted): 90–105 min, 35–40 km at 120–150W, cut short if HR > 145 bpm
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Cut to 30–40 min easy spin at 100–120W, flat route, strict HR cap of 135 bpm — treat as a systems-check ride only, not a training stimulus. Stop immediately if any illness symptoms resurface.
proposed_changes.reason: Body battery on 15 August is recorded at 0 and sleep has been critically disrupted for two weeks post-illness; the athlete-reported sick note (no sport until 11 Aug) means this is only day 4 back and the body is not ready for even a moderate aerobic ride.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk8 Long Run (AI adjusted): up to 54 min at 6:15–6:45/km, swim also planned
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Replace the run entirely with a 30–40 min easy walk or light open-water float/technique swim (no pacing targets); skip any structured run until at least Tuesday 18 August and only if sleep gate is met (6+ hrs, body battery ≥ 45 on waking).
proposed_changes.reason: Running the day after a return ride, less than a week out of illness with body battery at zero, risks relapse; the athlete-reported context explicitly noted doctor's advice to rest until 11 August and recovery is clearly still incomplete.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk9 Evening session: 4 x 1 km @ 5:45/km with 90-sec walk recovery, execute only if sleep gate met
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Retain the sleep gate condition strictly (6.5 h avg sleep 15–18 Aug AND body battery ≥ 50 on waking 18 Aug); if gate is NOT met, replace entirely with 20–25 min easy jog at 6:30–7:00/km with no structure. Do not attempt intervals until gate is confirmed.
proposed_changes.reason: Given the severity and duration of the sleep disruption through mid-August, the probability of the sleep gate being met on 18 August is low — building in a clear downgrade path prevents the athlete from pushing through intervals on inadequate recovery.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk9 Long Ride (AI adjusted): 60 min at 128–177W, with morning open-water swim added, ride reduced to 75–80 km
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Cap the ride at 60 min / ~35–40 km at 128–150W (lower half of Z2) with no morning swim added this week; save the swim-plus-ride brick format for week 10 once a full week of consistent sleep and training has been re-established.
proposed_changes.reason: Stacking a swim-brick onto a long ride in the first full training week back from illness adds unnecessary compounding load before baseline fitness has been re-confirmed.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk10 Long Ride (AI adjusted): 100 km at 128–177W; if no bike available abroad, replace with 75-min swim
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Explicitly plan for the no-bike scenario given the athlete is confirmed abroad 24–30 August: replace with a 75–90 min open-water or pool swim (2,200–2,500 m at 2:25–2:30/100m) as the primary session — this directly serves the Half Oceanman 5,000m swim target and should be treated as a priority, not a fallback.
proposed_changes.reason: Athlete-reported context confirms travel the week of 24 August; bike access abroad is uncertain, and proactively scheduling the swim replacement maximises Half Oceanman readiness (nearest race, 49 days away) rather than risking a missed long session.

proposed_changes.current_session: [AI ADDED] 60 min open-water evening swim (2,000–2,500 m) after the 100 km morning ride
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Skip the added evening swim on this date entirely — if the ride is replaced by a single morning swim (2,200–2,500 m) as proposed above, a second swim the same evening is excessive for a week still in recovery build; consolidate to one quality swim session of 75–90 min.
proposed_changes.reason: Doubling swim sessions on the same day during a travel week coming off illness risks fatigue accumulation without proportional fitness return, and the single longer swim already covers the Half Oceanman volume target for this week.
